decisions.rationale: All comparators were reviewed. The neighbors address stale config activation, broad skills mutation, or remote supply-chain trust; none has the same archive-import staging, atomic commit, partial-extraction cleanup, and validation-race boundary.

The browser neighbors cover URL-workspace binding, hidden automation sessions, or CEF runtime recovery, not normal-tab restore to a missing detached origin with the same fallback and disclosure outcome.

Capture-chip races, debugging ownership, and least-privilege browser control are adjacent to sharing, but they do not reproduce session-scoped sharing authority, chip mediation, separate commands, events, and recovery boundaries.

The broad skills umbrella and frontmatter-validation feature are related, but neither is equivalent to the exhaustive discovery and parser resource-bound contract spanning counts, depth, bytes, aliases, deadlines, cancellation, indexing, and backpressure.

Remote load ordering, duplicate validation, and compatibility-root conflicts are plausible neighbors, but none shares the within-recursive-root enumeration and git-root-versus-selected-project identity boundary.
The comparators concern hidden sessions, browser windowing, or CEF installation and updates. They do not define the positive browser-instance lifecycle and capacity model omitted by the LRU non-goal.

Exhaustive review found no comparator governing progress-widget drill payloads, authorization, historical binding, target deletion, navigation acknowledgement, keyboard behavior, and fallback as one state boundary.

Kubernetes recovery, preview races, named Docker anchors, and Docker-host state lists are adjacent operation families, but none matches destructive Docker command confirmation, partial failure, and recovery semantics.

The related capability records are media- or caller-visibility contracts. They do not share automation capability classes, typed availability and reason states, freshness, and consumer conformance authority.

Exact Firecrawl regeneration anchors and DRY anchor ownership are related governance controls, but neither supplies the inbound-link compatibility and alias-migration oracle required for section renumbering.
Web payloads and the web-provider capability mirror consume nearby operation truth, but they are not the canonical provider-operation matrix or its non-erasure rule for fetch support.

Media route tie-breaking and fallback are different product authorities, while the web capability mirror is an umbrella neighbor. None matches the web dispatcher's ordered adapter selection, retry-safe failure classes, exhaustion, provenance, and disclosure lifecycle.
Web payloads, web events, and UI-command seams are adjacent, but they do not reproduce the locked user-facing command identities and event families for web operations and Gist Review.
Route correlation and bounded open targets touch runtime identity, but neither owns the terminal, PTY promotion, dev-session, command-card evidence, and catalog mutation family as enumerated here.
Capability disclosure and web capability classes are related, but neither states the same provider-lineage boundary that excludes arbitrary code execution from first-class PM tools.

The comparator browser features cover narrower pause, hidden-session, engine, or privilege concerns. They are members or adjacent layers, not the same compaction-plus-browser-session command and event contract.

The neighbors expose owner edges, closure state, readiness quality, and SSOT seams in narrower or different domains. None is equivalent to a closed-world manifest of every expected caller, command, alias, retirement, owner, and machine-checkable result.

The Firecrawl reconciliation and ownership records are plausible neighbors, but they address document sets, routing closure, or field-level seams rather than the singular provider-owner authority and consumer deference contract.
MCP identity normalization and status reconciliation are separate records and state boundaries. Neither defines extract token-to-type interpretation or precedence among Core and owner authorities.
Tool envelopes, web payloads, and events carry evidence, but none has the same actual-read-path citation authority, strongest-provenance dedupe, and weak-snippet disclosure outcome.

Registry promotion, Kubernetes mutation, and media requests are concrete side-effecting members with their own authorities. They do not equal the cross-tool retry contract for idempotency class, request keys, executed-at-all evidence, and compensation.

Retired bridges, compatibility labels, extraction routing, and OpenCode non-equivalence preserve nearby governance boundaries, but none is the Tools owner map plus ContractRef consumer-placement rule.

The batch-event comparator is a member of this execution lifecycle, and general web events and provider routes are adjacent. None covers the same grants, concurrency, deadline, fail-fast cancellation, partial results, retry, and audit boundary end to end.
Other browser-session lifecycles are related by cleanup vocabulary, but they do not own Firecrawl interact TTL, crash cleanup, cleanup retry, or sensitive remote browser-state disposal.

The web-provider mirror includes DDG behavior among a broad set of route concerns, making it an umbrella neighbor; it is not equivalent to the bounded DDG no-key and optional-Google integration posture.

Fallback blocked reasons and the no-work terminal branch are taxonomy neighbors, but neither resolves post-execution validation against executed-at-all evidence and blocked-versus-failed classification.
Web payloads and provider capability routing are consumers or adjacent provider concerns; neither specifies the fixed partition flattening, source tagging, and web-news-images merge order.

MCP effective-state precedence is a different subsystem, and the web-provider mirror contains related Firecrawl configuration concerns. Neither defines the configured-versus-enabled Firecrawl transition table.

Lazy catalog search and explicit owner routing are related boundaries, but neither states the same falsifiable distinction between path candidate discovery and authoritative exact-content verification.
A mirrored grammar and formatter detection table have analogous drift risks but different product authorities. Neither is the referenced Tools policy order and registry-table binding required here.
The broad provider-route feature contains Tavily budgeting and other providers, but it does not equal the additive search-then-enrichment economics and Site Reader non-replacement boundary.

Canonical MCP identity and credential revocation are neighboring trust controls in different authorities. They do not cover canonical host normalization, redirect reauthorization, and host-display spoofing for mixed-host web session grants.

Registry promotion, Docker Manager ownership, and Unraid follow-on publication are adjacent commands or consumers. None expresses the shared remote-side-effect authority while preserving Orchestrator and Docker Manager as distinct commands.

The comparators cover component envelopes, events, browser privilege, or provider routes. They are members or neighbors, not the combined visible web-activity, bounded browser-action, schema-extraction validation, and noncanonical-format boundary.
Subagent context limits are operational resource controls, not the research role's read-only authority and coordinator-only ledger mutation and synthesis boundary.
Compatibility tiers and web capability classes are related vocabulary consumers, but neither is the complete canonical support-tier label set and pm-composed to pm_composed alias rule.

Web Error Taxonomy is the closest comparator, but it owns the canonical error envelope and broader meta requiredness, whereas this anchor owns Firecrawl adapter mapping, closest-class selection, and preservation of unmapped provider detail. The owner seam and state boundary keep them distinct.
Batch events, payloads, and broad provider routes are related consumers, but none is the Firecrawl operation-matrix coverage rule requiring both exact batch mappings.
Preview and capability-picker accessibility are distinct surfaces. They do not cover provider status disclosure names, non-color cues, focus, localization, and overflow as the same UI state boundary.

Web payloads and other session lifecycles are related layers, but none owns Site Reader page and session transitions, concurrent navigation, iframe failure, stale-page invalidation, and cleanup receipts.
Exhaustive comparison found no feature with the web change-tracking fresh-fetch state machine. Catalog refresh and generic provider failures use different records, authorities, and user outcomes.
Web payloads and provider route mirrors are adjacent, but neither owns the exact method-locked endpoint inventory or the typed-mapping gate against provider-only operations becoming PM tools.
Generic web payloads and provider-route concerns do not duplicate the webextract-specific one-URL-to-array mapping, JSON Schema mapping, and retained PM-side scope validation.

Obligation closure, Docker contract gaps, readiness-grade units, and SSOT adjudication are neighboring governance concerns, but none is the per-risk owner, dependency, phase, closure-state, and receipt contract.
Blocked-reason and terminal-branch records are adjacent runtime taxonomy, but neither binds skip_node and abort_run to confirmation strength and reversibility metadata.
Web payloads and provider configuration are related, but neither defines authority and safety checks for ignoreRobotsTxt, redirects, delay, large crawl limits, and target expansion.
The provider-route umbrella mentions Tavily resource policy but does not duplicate the user-facing Settings hierarchy for enablement, API key, priority, and Advanced options.

Credential, media route, account-label, and web-provider comparators are adjacent but use different authorities. None owns model-native websearch auth reuse, effective identity disclosure, and preservation of the PM websearch tool key.

Batch events, web events, and provider-route resource policy are related members, but none covers research-wide per-source timeout, network loss, retry, cancellation, partial results, and deterministic recovery.

Tool events, capture-chip races, evidence retention, and browser privilege are component concerns. They do not equal the combined element, selection, and screenshot artifact lifecycle with provenance, redaction, atomicity, retention, revocation, and hostile-DOM boundaries.

Preview races, paused and hidden sessions, CEF runtime recovery, and least-privilege control are narrower members or other layers. None spans preview creation through detach, close, reopen, retry, promotion, auth isolation, stop-agent, and crash recovery.

Debugging ownership, DevTools placement, and general browser privilege are related, but none matches the DevTools capability contract spanning environment support, role and privacy policy, dock layout, platform behavior, and no-persist boundaries.

Payloads, events, errors, and provider routes are constituent contracts. Under the strict umbrella/member rule they remain distinct from the chat operation family that combines normalized inputs with network, hostile-content, provenance, consent, retention, cancellation, and offline boundaries.

Registry promotion, preview start-stop, named Docker anchors, and Docker-host state lists are adjacent operations or umbrellas. None owns the build, bake, scan, and prune lifecycle with target selection, progress, cancellation, timeout, destructive preview, authority, and rollback.
